I am an old man of 76 years here in Shinyanga, and I have farmed this land my whole life without ever sitting in a school. My plot is big — over thirteen hectares — but the rains here are not always kind, and chemical fertilizer costs too much money for a man like me. I will put the cattle manure from my boma on the field like my father taught me, and I will plant the seeds I saved from last harvest, intercropping as I always do so that if one crop fails another will feed the household. My sons and grandchildren will help me work the land, and when the weeding and harvest come heavy I will call a few neighbors to help for a small payment.
